chapter_theme: The one song at Thirukkonamalai (திருக்கோணமலை) in Lanka: the poet confesses drowning in desire for women who sell their bodies, mocked by the world and sick in a body of filth, and asks to be saved by singing Murugan in verse; the praise makes Murugan the meaning that comes alive in the verses of the sages and Tamil poets.

650.reading: The poet confesses that, drowning in desire for women who glitter with girdles and jewels on bodies put up for sale, he became the great lustful man the world laughs at, toiling and exhausted, and asks Murugan, the one life who lets him cross over by telling him in verse, not to let him suffer in disease in this cage of filth, but to look with grace on the dog who seeks and praises him and give him the grace of his feet. The praise names the son of Sivakami's lord, the six-faced teacher, the one who comes as the meaning in the verses of Vasishtha, Kashyapa, the yogis, Agastya, Idaikkadar and Keeran, who comes to the gopuram gateway at Thirukkonamalai, and whose vel powdered the sea of seven births.
650.nuance: விலைக்கு மேனி: the women's bodies are 'for a price', so the courtesan's trade is named. உனைக் கவிக்குள்ளாய்ச் சொலிக் கடைத்தேறவே: the way out is to put the god into verse. வகுத்த பாவினில் பொருட்கோலமாய் வரு: Murugan is the meaning-form that comes in the poems of the sages and of Tamil poets such as Idaikkadar and Nakkirar (கீரன்). The words about parrots and பூதி at the gopuram gate are obscure.

source_issues: Song 650: one corrupt character in மயலு஡றி (line 259), probably மயலூறி.
Song 649, filed under Kathirkamam, closes on அருக்கொணாமலை and may belong to this shrine.
